summary.text: Alison White is the Family First candidate for Shepparton at the 2026 Victorian election, as listed by the ABC and on the party's Victorian candidate list. Neither the party nor the ABC had published a biography of her as at early November 2026. Someone of the same name stood for Family First Victoria in Shepparton in 2022; the sources don't say whether it is the same person.

previous_candidacies.note: The ABC's 2022 Shepparton results list an Alison White for Family First Victoria; no source confirms she is the 2026 candidate.

sources.title: Shepparton: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Victorian Election, Family First Party Australia

summary.text: Cayla Fin is Labor's candidate for Shepparton at the 2026 Victorian election. Her career of more than 15 years has been in TAFE and university education, most recently as TAFE Victoria's regional lead for Shepparton. She lives in Dookie, and her party says her own treatment for breast cancer underlies her focus on health care close to home.

priorities.text: Health care available close to home, which she links to her own experience of breast cancer
Strong local services for families in the Goulburn Valley
Rural and regional communities getting the same opportunities as the rest of the state

sources.title: Shepparton: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Grace Verney is the Greens candidate for Shepparton at the 2026 Victorian election. She studies at university while working full time in the health sector. She says she grew up on a low income in regional Victoria, and her campaign centres on health care, living costs, gender equality and justice for First Nations people.

occupation.text: Health sector worker and university student

priorities.text: I believe everyone should have access to the essentials they need
Health services that keep up with Shepparton's growing, varied population
Taking gender equality and First Nations justice seriously

summary.text: Karen Hocking is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Shepparton at the 2026 Victorian election. A nurse and long-time Shepparton resident, she has volunteered for years as an administrator with the Shepparton Junior Soccer Association. In 2022 she headed the party's upper-house ticket in Northern Victoria, which did not win a seat.

priorities.text: I believe that people are more important than profit.
Free health care, including aged care and disability services, open to all
A free bus service in Shepparton good enough to replace driving
Affordable housing for the city's renters and mortgage holders
Staffed community spaces and libraries with longer hours in regional towns

sources.title: Shepparton: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Lou Costa is an independent candidate for Shepparton at the 2026 Victorian election, with the backing of the Voices for Goulburn Valley group. Raised in Shepparton East, she trained in landscape architecture at RMIT. She came back to the region in 1998 to set up her own business, Design By Nature, and has worked with construction firms in the electorate.

sources.title: Shepparton: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Phillip Bryant is One Nation's candidate for Shepparton at the 2026 Victorian election. According to the ABC, his career includes seven and a half years of military service in the ADF, a decade as joint owner of a family business and close to 20 years managing retail stores. One Nation's candidate page could not be read for this profile.

prior_roles.role: Member of the Australian Defence Force

sources.title: Shepparton: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Shane Sali is the Nationals candidate for Shepparton at the 2026 Victorian election, where the party's sitting MP, Kim O'Keeffe, is not recontesting. Born and raised in Shepparton, he won a seat on the city council in 2020 and became mayor in 2022, and he chaired Regional Cities Victoria from 2023 to 2025. Before council he worked in local businesses, including as an accounts manager at a Telstra business centre.

occupation.note: The ABC and the Nationals describe his council service, but neither says whether he still holds the seat.

prior_roles.note: The ABC gives the year he was elected; no source says whether he is still a councillor.
The ABC gives the year he became mayor; no source says whether he still holds the post.

previous_candidacies.note: No source gives the label he ran under at the council election.

priorities.text: I will fight for better healthcare closer to home, a better road network
Better local sports facilities and a fairer bus network
Action on water security, crime and road safety
